subject: Proposed invoice smoothing + deposit structure (VAT flow question)
messages:
From: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@lacunatx.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: procure@lacunatx.com
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Invoice cadence + deposit ask (VAT flow)

Hi Olga,

Hope you're well. We're putting the final finance plan together for our pilot and have a couple of asks related to invoicing and tax treatment: 

1) We'd like to smooth invoices over the first 90 days (3 equal invoices) rather than one large upfront invoice to match our monthly supplier cadence.
2) Lacuna would be able to provide a 20% refundable deposit at contract signature to secure the capacity, rather than prepaying 100%.
3) We need clarity on where VAT will be charged — Lacuna is UK-registered but the paying entity is in the US; finance needs the vendor VAT certificate or guidance on reverse-charge applicability.

Can Redwood confirm whether you can: (a) issue three invoiced milestones (30/60/90 days) tied to seat delivery, (b) accept a 20% deposit with the remainder on the staggered invoices, and (c) send any VAT documentation or recommended treatment for our tax team?

If helpful, I attached a short worksheet with the amounts we expect. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call this week.

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Kim
Senior Procurement Manager
Lacuna Therapeutics
procure@lacunatx.com

Attachment: Lacuna_invoice_plan.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@lacunatx.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice cadence + deposit ask (VAT flow)

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear note and the worksheet. Short answer: yes, we can accommodate a staggered invoicing plan and a refundable deposit, but there are a couple of operational details to align on VAT and credit buffer.

Proposed approach: 
- Contract signature: 20% refundable deposit (Redwood issues a receipt; deposit held against first invoice).
- Day 0 delivery: invoice #1 for 30% net -30 (first of three; deposit offsets amount due).
- Day 30: invoice #2 for 25% net-30.
- Day 60: invoice #3 for remaining 25% net-30.

Why these numbers? We want to keep an on-paper deposit to protect capacity while keeping per-invoice amounts aligned to monthly forecast. The deposit will be refunded after invoice #3 clears unless there are outstanding credits.

VAT/tax: Since Lacuna is UK-registered but payment originates from a US entity, we usually ask for the customer's VAT registration certificate if they expect zero-rating or reverse-charge. If the paying entity is US-based and Redwood invoices our US entity, standard US sales tax rules apply (we don't charge UK VAT). If Lacuna needs Redwood to invoice a UK entity, we will need the VAT certificate and may apply reverse charge. Can you confirm which legal entity will sign and pay? I'll loop finance to provide the exact template for VAT evidence (we can accept the HMRC VAT registration extract PDF).

Next steps: 
- If you confirm the paying entity and approve the proposed invoice split, Marissa will draft the invoice schedule and the deposit receipt flow.
- Rishi will run a quick credit-limit check and flag any holdbacks.

We can also do a 20-minute call tomorrow.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com

Attachment: none

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 14:21:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Lacuna payment plan — credit/ops notes

Olga / Rishi,

Quick internal note after reviewing Daniel's worksheet:
- If we accept 20% refundable deposit, ops will need a clear refund trigger (we normally refund after final invoice is paid + 7 business days). Recommend documenting in SOW.
- Rishi — can you confirm Lacuna's current credit limit with us? I see prior POC activity but no formal credit history. If we keep the deposit, we can proceed at standard net-30 for subsequent invoices; otherwise consider net-45 for second/third invoice until credit clears.
- VAT: ask Lacuna to supply VAT_certificate_UK.pdf or HMRC extract; if their paying entity is in US, mark invoices to Redwood US entity (no UK VAT). If they insist on UK invoicing, finance needs to treat as cross-border (reverse charge) and we must collect certificate + signed SOW.

Also suggest adding a small early-pay discount (0.5% if paid within 10 days) to encourage timely payment and reduce our AR exposure. Thoughts?

-Marissa
Director, Customer Finance
Redwood Inference

3) Invoice B (30 days later): 25% of MRR; net-30 payment.
4) Invoice C (60 days later): 25% of MRR; net-30 payment.

Refund mechanics: Deposit refund issued 7 business days after Invoice C payment clears, unless there are outstanding disputes. We'll reference the SOW clause for refund triggers.

If this looks good I can send the SOW addendum and the three invoicing milestones to your finance team to process.
